title: Inside Sink Drainage: How Traps and Arms Work
description: A properly functioning sink drainage system relies on gravity, precise component geometry, and hydraulic principles to remove wastewater safely while blocking sewer gases from entering the building. The P-trap is a critical component that retains a water seal, preventing harmful gases from escaping through the fixture opening. Downstream of the trap, the drain arm directs wastewater toward the vertical stack at a consistent grade to ensure self-cleansing velocity. Mastering how these components interact helps technicians diagnose common issues like siphonage, gurgling, and slow drainage with absolute confidence.
